assessment_role.future_use: Only as a separately preregistered unknown-history diagnostic; never as a negative reference, controlled-positive parent, or accuracy denominator.

provider_findings.final_release_format: one-second-or-shorter mono 16 kHz signed 16-bit integer PCM WAV
provider_findings.open_site_release_conversion: FFmpeg decoded OGG and resampled the result to 16 kHz PCM WAV
provider_findings.other_source_path: varying-sample-rate WAV inputs resampled to 16 kHz with a similar FFmpeg command
provider_findings.speaker_identity: stable hashed eight-hex-digit identifier derived from web-session or other-source speaker identifiers

rejection_basis: The primary paper says the WebAudioAPI returned OGG-compressed audio and the server stored those OGG files.
The paper says the majority of the dataset came from that open-site path.
The release pipeline decoded the OGG files and resampled them to 16 kHz PCM WAV, so the current WAV wrapper does not establish no-lossy history.
Other inputs followed a different WAV-resampling path, but the documented release schema does not expose a per-file path field.
The pre-OGG PCM, exact OGG codec, encoder implementation, settings, and per-file capture path are not bound, so the files cannot form controlled positives either.
